papers.title_en: Enabling Extended SGX Enclaves inside Confidential Virtual Machines
papers.authors: Pamenas Kariuki, Dong Yiliang, Quoc Do Le, Christof Fetzer
papers.evidence: 在机密虚拟机内嵌套SGX飞地实现TEE隔离
papers.tldr: 机密虚拟机（CVM，如AMD SEV-SNP）与进程级enclave（如Intel SGX）分别提供云负载保护，但在TCB、部署成本、资源隔离和编程模型上差异显著，将SGX嵌套进CVM可互补，却面临缺乏enclave内部保护、切换与异常路径昂贵、克隆慢、编程受限等问题。TEEVisor是一种驻留CVM的架构，含安全监视器与内核驱动，利用AMD SEV-SNP的VMPL在客户CVM内构建硬件保护的进程级enclave，并支持SGX二进制兼容模式和新eSGX扩展模式。在商用AMD EPYC上，相对原生CVM，计算与内存负载开销低于5%，I/O密集应用约12%，enclave克隆速度达93 μs/MB。该工作证明在CVM内实现扩展SGX语义兼具兼容性、性能与可编程性，适合生产使用。
papers.abstract_en: Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs), such as AMD SEV-SNP, and process enclaves, such as Intel SGX, provide workload protection against cloud threats. However, they strongly differ in TCB, deployment cost and speed, peer workload protection, resource sharing, fine-grained isolation and attestation, and programming capabilities. Nesting process enclaves within CVMs offers an optimal solution and an opportunity to address long-standing SGX limitations: lack of intra-enclave protection, expensive transitions and exception paths, slow enclave cloning, and a restricted programming model that limits Library Operating Systems (LibOS).   This paper introduces TEEVisor, a CVM-resident architecture consisting of a security monitor and a kernel driver that leverages AMD SEV-SNP Virtual Machine Privilege Levels (VMPLs) to build hardware-protected, process-level enclaves inside a guest CVM with two modes: (1) an SGX binary compatibility mode to run unmodified SGX applications; and (2) a novel extended SGX~(eSGX) mode optimizing slow execution paths and offering richer enclave programming capabilities. On commercial AMD EPYC hardware, against native CVM execution, TEEVisor incurs under 5% overhead on compute- and memory-bound workloads, around 12% on I/O-heavy applications, and accelerates enclave cloning to a rate of 93~$μ$s/MB of enclave size, demonstrating that eSGX semantics inside a CVM are practical for production use.

papers.title_en: Learning from Failures: A Failure-Driven Prompt Refinement for LLM-Based Vulnerability Analysis
papers.evidence: 面向LLM漏洞分析的失败驱动提示精炼
papers.tldr: 大语言模型用于软件漏洞分析时，效果高度依赖提示设计，但现有研究多比较总体指标，难以解释失败原因并系统改进提示。为此，作者提出失败驱动提示精炼（FDPR），先在DVJA上归纳假阳性、假阴性、无依据推理和CWE误分类等重复失败模式，再将其转化为针对性提示修改。随后在Juliet测试集评估并做跨模型验证，结果显示该方法提升了漏洞分析可靠性，并提炼出可复用提示设计原则。该工作把重复失败作为提示工程基础，推动更可靠的LLM漏洞分析系统。
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models have emerged as promising tools for software vulnerability analysis, but their effectiveness depends heavily on prompt design. Existing research primarily compares prompting strategies using aggregate performance metrics, providing limited insight into why models fail or how prompts can be improved systematically. We propose Failure-Driven Prompt Refinement (FDPR), a methodology that analyzes recurring model failures to guide evidence-based prompt refinement. Using the Damn Vulnerable Java Application (DVJA), we identify recurring failure modes, including false positives, false negatives, unsupported reasoning, and CWE misclassification, and translate them into targeted prompt refinements. We then evaluate the resulting prompt on the Juliet Test Suite and perform cross-model validation to assess generalizability. The results show that failure-driven refinement improves the reliability of LLM-based vulnerability analysis while yielding reusable prompt design principles. More broadly, this work demonstrates that recurring model failures provide a principled foundation for prompt engineering, enabling the systematic development of more reliable LLM-based vulnerability analysis systems.

papers.title_en: A Systematic Study of Security Enforcement at Android Inter-Component Boundaries
papers.evidence: Android边界安全执行缺口的系统性研究
papers.tldr: Android 组件间通信边界是应用与系统的主要接口，其安全执行是否按设计生效尚缺系统评估。本文在 Android 17 上对 30 多个 Google/AOSP 包开展 120 项评估，以零权限攻击者模型下的期望-观察框架检验五类接口。结果发现 97 处执行缺口（80.8%）与 23 处有效执行（19.2%），Activity 与 BroadcastReceiver 缺口率 100%，ContentProvider 仅 27.6% 生效。据此提出 14 类缺口分类法，并揭示平台安全变更被禁用及 18 个敏感 URI scheme 注册。
papers.abstract_en: Android's inter-process communication (IPC) mechanisms (Activities, Services, BroadcastReceivers, ContentProviders, and URI scheme handlers) form the primary interface between applications and between applications and the system. We present a systematic study of security enforcement comprising 120 evaluations (99 inter-component interface evaluations across five interface categories, 10 platform security-control evaluations, and 11 dedicated positive controls) in over 30 Google and AOSP packages on Android 17 (API 37). Using an expected-versus-observed framework under a zero-permission attacker model, we evaluate whether each boundary's enforcement mechanism functions as designed. We find 97 enforcement gaps (80.8%) and 23 enforcement holds (19.2%). From these observations, we derive a 14-category enforcement gap taxonomy organized across manifest, code, platform, and architectural layers. Within our purposively selected corpus, observed enforcement outcomes differ substantially across interface categories: evaluated Activities and BroadcastReceivers exhibit a 100% gap rate, while ContentProviders, which benefit from framework-provided defenses such as setStrict(), achieve a 27.6% holds rate. We find that all seven evaluated platform compatibility changes with security intent are either disabled or gated at a targetSdkVersion that none of the applications in our evaluated corpus targets. We document 18 custom URI scheme registrations handling sensitive data (authentication tokens, payment credentials, medical information) despite the known unverifiability of custom schemes (RFC 8252 Section 8.1). Our study includes 23 positive controls, calibration cases demonstrating that the evaluation procedure distinguishes functioning enforcement from observed enforcement failures.

papers.title_en: ContractLens: Latent Security Knowledge for Malicious Smart Contract Detection
papers.authors: Shuyi Miao, Xinyi Huang, Wangjie Qiu, Fei Shen, Jinchun He, Zhiming Zheng, Tat-Seng Chua
papers.evidence: 利用潜在安全知识进行恶意智能合约检测
papers.tldr: 恶意智能合约威胁Web3.0安全，但现有LLM审计多靠提示工程或特定微调，内部检测恶意逻辑的表征仍不清楚。ContractLens通过逐层线性探针筛选对恶意逻辑敏感且稳定的关键层，并以激活对比、恶意逻辑特异性和探针权重评分，按拐点自适应选择MCDU。拼接这些单元激活训练轻量分类器，预训练模型全程冻结。实验显示掩码MCDU导致更大性能下降，平均检测准确率优于对比方法，并能泛化未见恶意意图、支持少样本检测。
papers.abstract_en: Detecting malicious smart contracts is essential to safeguarding the Web3.0 ecosystem. However, existing auditing methods based on large language models (LLMs) largely rely on prompt engineering or attack-specific fine-tuning, while the internal representations that support malicious logic detection remain poorly characterized. To address this gap, we propose ContractLens, a framework that localizes and uses latent security knowledge in pretrained LLMs for interpretable malicious smart contract detection. Specifically, we first use layerwise linear probes to identify candidate layers that distinguish malicious from benign contracts, then select critical layers based on their sensitivity to malicious logic removal and stability under behaviour-preserving surface modifications. Next, within these critical layers, we combine activation contrast, malicious-logic specificity, and probe weights into a tri-factor importance score and adaptively select malicious contract-discriminative units (MCDUs) using the knee point of the ranked score curve. Finally, we concatenate the selected units' activations into a compact representation and train a lightweight classifier for detection, keeping the pretrained model frozen throughout. Neuron masking experiments show that masking MCDUs causes larger drops in detection performance than masking randomly selected neurons or neurons matched in activation magnitude. ContractLens achieves higher average detection accuracy than the evaluated methods on all three pretrained models. Further evaluations demonstrate generalization to unseen malicious intents and show that, with the identified MCDUs fixed, a classifier trained on few labelled samples can still achieve strong detection performance.

papers.title_en: Security Is More Than a Library Call: How Security Features Live in Code
papers.authors: Kevin Hermann, Sven Peldszus, Thorsten Berger
papers.evidence: 访问控制与密码学等安全特性在代码中的实现
papers.tldr: 安全功能实现困难，已有研究多基于调研访谈，缺乏代码层面全系统理解。本文对9个大型开源Java系统开展挖掘研究，人工检查212万行代码、19121个文件，标注183395行、561个安全功能，映射到54类。研究揭示安全功能在代码中的真实形态，并强调集成工作不可忽视：结果显示安全功能远非调用外部库，常体积庞大、散布全代码库并相互纠缠；外部库虽常用，但集成需大量代码。这为安全功能设计与工具支持提供实证基础。
papers.abstract_en: Implementing security features---functionalities that protect sensitive data or prevent malicious actions by attackers---is important for ensuring the security and integrity of software systems. Correctly implementing access control, cryptography, or other security features is challenging as they require substantial domain expertise, careful design, and custom implementation to integrate them within the software system.   Previous work has thoroughly studied security awareness, perception, practices, and expertise via surveys, interviews, and experiments. While they have shown that the implementation of security features are often supported by security libraries and frameworks, they have also shown that developers rarely are security experts, and make mistakes that introduce vulnerabilities into software when using them. Despite this extensive knowledge of security practices and developer behavior, we still lack a comprehensive understanding of how security features actually manifest at the code level across full software systems.   We close this gap by conducting a mining study of security features in 9 popular and large open-source Java systems. We manually inspected 2,127,761 lines of code across 19,121 files, identifying and annotating 183,395 lines implementing 561 security features corresponding to 54 security features in our taxonomy. We analyzed the characteristics of the identified security features, such as their size, scattering, tangling, common implementation patterns, and the use of internal and external functionalities. Our findings show that security features are far more than mere calls to external libraries. Security features, such as access control, can grow large in size, scatter across the whole codebase, and frequently tangle with each other. External security libraries are commonly used, but they require substantial amounts of code for integration.

papers.title_en: ToFu: Exploiting and Fuzzing the LLM-Orchestrator-Tool Trust Boundary
papers.authors: Md Nazmul Islam Ananto, Pierre Prevost-Avenel, Colin Smith, Kyungtae Kim, Taegyu Kim, Arslan Khan
papers.evidence: 在LLM-工具信任边界进行模糊测试与语义安全检查
papers.tldr: LLM 智能体通过工具调用外部软件时，编排层把模型输出转为结构化调用，形成 LLM-编排器-工具信任边界，但工具语义常未被强制执行，LLM 生成的参数易被误当可信。ToFu 据此自动从工具元数据和 CWE 引导的清洗器语料中派生语义安全检查，并借助运行时内省与结果净化生成模糊测试 harness 和语义 oracle。在 273 个 MCP 服务器、3405 个工具上评估，发现 118 个服务器中 343 个工具存在对应 CWE 类别的已验证缺陷。这表明现实工具普遍不校验文档化输入语义，不能默认信任 LLM 生成的参数。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as agents that interact with external software through tools, with an orchestration layer translating model outputs into structured tool invocations. This architecture creates an LLM-orchestrator-tool trust boundary where tool semantics may go unenforced and LLM-generated arguments may be incorrectly treated as trusted. We present ToFu, a tool-aware framework that automatically derives semantic security checks for LLM tools from their existing metadata and a CWE-guided sanitizer corpus. ToFu specializes these checks to individual tools and automatically generates fuzzing harnesses and semantic oracles using runtime introspection and outcome sanitization. We evaluated ToFu across 273 MCP servers containing 3405 tools and identified verified bugs corresponding to CWE weakness classes in 343 tools across 118 of the servers. Our findings show that real-world tools frequently fail to enforce their documented input semantics, making it unsafe to treat LLM-generated arguments as trusted.
